metaDescription: Five budget kitchen scissors sets at the lowest tier, compared on blade thickness, pack size, sheaths and cleaning so you know what a tight budget buys.
introParagraphs: At the lowest price tier, kitchen scissors stop being a single tool and become a small pack. Four of the five picks here are multi-packs, and the one single pair is the only option from a household kitchenware name. That changes how you shop: you are not just choosing a blade, you are choosing how many spares, how much sheath protection, and how easy it is to keep a raw-meat pair away from a herb pair.

We evaluated each listing on blade thickness where the maker states it, handle coating, whether a cover or sheath is included, and how the set is meant to be cleaned. What you give up at this tier is mostly information and refinement. Few listings publish a steel hardness or a pivot design, and none of the five advertises a take-apart pivot, so deep cleaning after raw poultry depends on rinsing and drying carefully.

Spending more adds either a take-apart design, thicker blades for bone and joint work, or a gadget-style tool. This guide shows what each of the five does well at the cap, where each one runs out of road, and which pick suits a first apartment, a gift drawer, or a household that wants separate shears for separate jobs.

products.name: iBayam 2-Pack Kitchen Scissors, 8.66 in
products.description:
The iBayam 2-pack is built around 8.66 inch all-purpose shears with hardened stainless steel blades that the listing says will handle cardboard, twine, poultry, meat and vegetables. Each pair ships with a protective sheath and a soft comfort-grip handle coating, and the maker mentions cushioning pads on the handles.

The real draw at this tier is the second pair. One can live by the stove and the other in a junk drawer for packaging and twine, which keeps the kitchen pair from going dull on cardboard. That is a bigger practical win than any steel claim, because dullness from non-food use is what ruins most budget shears.

Ownership is simple: slide on the sheath after each use, wash by hand, and dry the pivot. Compared with the SZHLUX at 2.5mm thick, the iBayam does not publish a blade thickness, so treat it as a light to medium duty pair rather than a bone cutter. It is also a safer bet for general use than the KitchenAid single pair if you value having a spare more than a brand name.
products.bestFor: Households that want a spare pair and a sheath on each pair without spending beyond the cap.

products.name: SZHLUX 2-Pack Heavy Duty Kitchen Scissors
products.description:
SZHLUX is the one pick that publishes its blade thickness: 2.5mm stainless steel, which the listing contrasts with traditional 1.5mm blades. That thicker blade is the single most useful spec to see at this tier because thin blades flex when they meet chicken joints, cartilage or a stubborn wrapper.

The listing claims the shears can handle food, fish, meat, bones and poultry, and mentions pizza, pasta and nut cracking. Treat the bone claim cautiously. Poultry shears made for joints are usually thicker still, so think of these as a sturdy general pair that can part a chicken but will not match a dedicated spring-loaded tool.

Cleaning is a plus, since the maker allows either hand washing or the dishwasher and includes a protective cover. Against the iBayam, you get a more specific build claim and the same two-pair value. The tradeoff is that a thicker blade often means a heavier feel in hand, and the listing does not describe a take-apart pivot, so rinse the joint well after raw poultry.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want the sturdiest-looking blade at the cap for chicken and meat prep.
pros: 2.5mm blades published in the listing
Two pairs in one pack
Dishwasher safe or hand wash
Protective cover for storage
cons: Bone claims are broader than a 2.5mm blade suggests

products.name: Astercook 3-Pack Heavy Duty Kitchen Scissors
products.description:
Astercook gives you three pairs, each with a different handle color, so you can assign one to meat and seafood, one to vegetables, and one to herbs. The listing frames the set as heavy-duty all-purpose shears for poultry, meat, herbs and vegetables, with a solid, sturdy feel.

Color-coding is the feature that matters at this budget because it solves cross-contamination without buying anything extra. The maker does not publish blade thickness or steel grade, so you are trusting the build rather than a spec. If you want a number to compare, the SZHLUX at 2.5mm is the only pick here that offers one.

In daily use a three-pack is easiest in a house where more than one person cooks. Hand each cook a color and nobody has to guess which pair touched raw chicken. Compared with the OMDAR set, which also has three pairs, Astercook leaves the color assignment up to you, while OMDAR names specific colors for specific food types.
products.bestFor: Shared kitchens that want a separate pair for each type of food.
pros: Three pairs for the same budget as two-packs
Different handle color on each pair
Intended for poultry, meat, herbs and vegetables
Good for gifting or a second kitchen
cons: No published blade thickness or steel grade
Color use is left for the buyer to assign

products.name: OMDAR 3-Pack Stainless Steel Kitchen Shears
products.description:
OMDAR ships three pairs with a defined system: red for raw meat, gray for cooked food, and orange for fruits and vegetables. The listing says this dedicated use helps keep raw and cooked foods separate, which is the most food-safety-minded design among the five picks.

The handles are PP plus TPR, an ergonomic non-slip combination meant for repeated use, and the listing also pitches the shears for seafood work on lobsters and crabs. The maker does not state a blade thickness, so shell-cracking expectations should stay modest.

Against the Astercook, OMDAR makes the decision for you, which suits a cook who does not want to invent a system. Against the single KitchenAid pair, you give up a recognizable name but gain two extra pairs. Check the product page for sheath or cover details, since the listing text we evaluated does not mention a protective cover. Handle feel is the other thing to check, since PP+TPR grips behave differently from the soft coatings on the iBayam pairs.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants a ready-made raw, cooked and produce separation.

Three pairs included
PP+TPR non-slip handles

cons: Cover or sheath not stated in the listing

products.name: KitchenAid All Purpose Kitchen Shears with Sheath
products.description:
The KitchenAid is the only single pair here, and the only one that advertises micro serrated edges. Those fine serrations help the blades grip slippery items like chicken skin or a wet herb bunch, which cuts down on slipping, and the stainless steel is described as built to resist rust.

The soft, non-slip coated handle is designed for extended use, and the pair is dishwasher safe and includes a protective sheath. That combination makes it the most low-maintenance pick for a person who wants one reliable pair rather than a stack.

The tradeoff is arithmetic. For roughly the same budget tier you could own two or three pairs from iBayam, SZHLUX, Astercook or OMDAR. Choose the KitchenAid when you value serrated grip and a known kitchenware brand over quantity, and when you do not need color-coding. It does not publish a blade thickness either, so keep it for everyday kitchen work rather than regular joint cutting.
products.bestFor: A single, simple pair with serrated grip and dishwasher-safe cleanup.
pros: Micro serrated blades grip slippery food
Dishwasher safe
Protective sheath included
Soft non-slip handle coating
cons: Only one pair for the budget

buyingCriteria.explanation: Thin blades bend against cartilage and joints, which is why the thickness figure is the one spec worth hunting for. Poultry-specific shears are often around 3.5mm, and general kitchen shears are usually thinner. Among these five, only the SZHLUX states a number, 2.5mm, and the listing contrasts it with traditional 1.5mm blades. If a listing gives no thickness, as with the iBayam, Astercook, OMDAR and KitchenAid picks, treat it as a light to medium duty pair.

At this budget the question is whether you want depth or a name. The iBayam and SZHLUX come as 2-packs, the Astercook and OMDAR as 3-packs, and the KitchenAid is one pair. A spare pair is the easiest way to protect the food pair from cardboard and twine, which dull edges fast. A single pair makes sense only if you will not use it for anything but cooking.

Loose shears in a drawer are a cut risk and the tips can chip against other tools. The iBayam and KitchenAid list protective sheaths, and the SZHLUX lists a protective cover. The OMDAR and Astercook listings we evaluated do not mention one, so check the page if drawer storage matters. A sheath is worth more than it sounds when you reach into a crowded utensil drawer without looking.

Micro serrations hold onto slippery skin and wet herbs, while plain sharp edges give cleaner cuts on paper and string. The KitchenAid is the only listing that advertises micro serrated edges. The others describe sharp stainless blades. If most of your cutting is chicken skin, bacon or herbs, the serrated edge removes a real source of slipping.

Raw poultry residue hides in pivots, so how a pair is cleaned matters. The KitchenAid is listed as dishwasher safe and the SZHLUX allows hand wash or dishwasher. None of the five advertises a take-apart pivot, which is a feature you find a tier higher. Rinse the pivot with hot soapy water after raw meat and dry it, because trapped moisture shortens the life of budget steel.

A soft or textured handle matters most for wet hands and for people who cut for long stretches. The OMDAR uses PP+TPR ergonomic handles, the iBayam and KitchenAid use soft coatings, and the Astercook is described as sturdy without a grip material named. Hold the pair in the store if you can, or look for return terms, because handle shape suits some hand sizes better than others. The KitchenAid is the only listing that frames its handle specifically for extended use, which matters if you break down whole chickens.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade and build claims
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each listing for stated blade thickness, steel type and edge style. Only the SZHLUX gives a thickness, at 2.5mm, and only the KitchenAid names micro serrations. Where a maker did not state something, we scored it as unknown rather than assuming it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value per pair
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how many usable pairs each purchase delivers. The Astercook and OMDAR lead at three pairs, the iBayam and SZHLUX deliver two, and the KitchenAid delivers one. A single pair needed a clear feature advantage to rank on par with a multi-pack.

howWeEvaluated.title: Storage and safety
howWeEvaluated.description: Protective sheaths or covers were weighed, since loose blades in a drawer are the most common source of kitchen scissor accidents. The iBayam, SZHLUX and KitchenAid list a sheath or cover, while the OMDAR and Astercook listings did not mention one.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and hygiene
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at dishwasher claims and whether color-coding helps separate raw and cooked food. OMDAR defines red, gray and orange roles, and Astercook offers three different colors. None advertises a take-apart pivot.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The SZHLUX leads on published blade thickness, the OMDAR on a ready-made food-safety system, the Astercook on pairs per set, the iBayam on a balance of sheath and spare, and the KitchenAid on edge type and brand. We did not claim hands-on durability, so all rankings rest on specs and the way each set is described.

cards.label: Multi-pack
cards.text: The iBayam, SZHLUX, Astercook and OMDAR give 2 to 3 pairs. You get spares, a dedicated cardboard pair and, with the Astercook and OMDAR, color separation. The downside is less brand information and uneven specs. Pick a multi-pack if you want redundancy.

cards.label: Single pair
cards.text: The KitchenAid is one pair with micro serrated edges, a sheath and dishwasher-safe cleanup. You pay for the name and fewer unknowns, not for more steel. Pick it if you only need one reliable pair.

faq.q: Which pick should I buy if I only want one?
faq.a: Choose the KitchenAid All Purpose Kitchen Shears if you want a single pair with micro serrated edges, a sheath and dishwasher cleanup. Choose the iBayam 2-Pack if you would rather have two pairs than one. If poultry is your main use, the SZHLUX at 2.5mm is the one with a published thickness.

faq.q: Are cheap kitchen scissors good enough?
faq.a: For everyday cooking, yes, as long as you expect light to medium work. Parting cooked chicken, trimming herbs, opening packages and cutting twine are all within reach. Dedicated bone and joint work wants thicker blades, often around 3.5mm in poultry shears.

faq.q: Can I put these in the dishwasher?
faq.a: The KitchenAid is listed as dishwasher safe and the SZHLUX allows hand wash or dishwasher. For the iBayam, Astercook and OMDAR, check the product page, because the listing text we evaluated does not confirm it. Hand washing is the safer default for any budget steel.

It helps when you remember to follow it. OMDAR assigns red to raw meat, gray to cooked food and orange to fruits and vegetables, so the roles are built in. Astercook gives three different handle colors, so you pick the rule. Either way, keep raw-meat shears out of the cooked-food zone.

faq.q: Why do the scissors get dull, and can I sharpen them?
faq.a: Using the food pair on cardboard, twine or plastic packaging is the usual cause. Steel in this class is typically a 3Cr13 or similar stainless, which can be sharpened with a wet stone if you want to extend its life. The easiest fix is a dedicated spare pair, which is why the multi-packs here are useful.

faq.q: What does spending more actually add?
faq.a: The next tier up tends to add three things: a pivot that comes apart for cleaning, blades closer to 3.5mm for joints, and extras such as a herb stripper or bottle opener. None of the five picks here advertises a take-apart pivot. If you only cook casually, those additions rarely change dinner, so the SZHLUX or OMDAR is a sensible stopping point.

faq.q: Do these work for lobster or crab?
faq.a: The OMDAR listing says it can be used for seafood such as lobsters and crabs. Expect shell snipping rather than heavy cracking, since no thickness is stated. For tough shells a thicker, dedicated tool does the job with less hand strain.
